# Using Drovr

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, ignore this
reflex — it is for the human-facing agent, not for you. Do your task.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

## What this is

This is your **always-on router**. Drovr is a working **discipline**, not just an
orchestration engine, and it is your default operating mode. This skill does not
do the work — it tells you *how* to work and *when* a task has outgrown one
context and must become its own phase.

Drovr exists because model output degrades as a context window fills (Chroma's
*context rot*, trychroma.com/research/context-rot). A fresh, tight context beats
a long one. Everything below serves that.

## The principle (always)

**Single writer, read-only explorers.** One agent edits at a time. Fan-out
investigation goes to read-only explorers (e.g. `explore-mcp`), never to parallel
writers. This holds whether you stay inline or escalate to phases.

**Always review.** Any change you write gets reviewed before you call it done —
invoke **`drovr:code-review`** (read-only review subagents; they find, you fix).
This is not optional and not gated on the change's size; it runs whether you
worked inline or across phases.

## For the task in front of you, apply the right methodology skill

Pick by what you are doing — invoke it via the `Skill` tool before you act:

- Implementing a feature or bugfix → **`drovr:tdd`** (test-first, watch it fail).
- Chasing a bug, test failure, or unexpected behavior → **`drovr:systematic-debugging`**.
- About to claim something is done/fixed/passing → **`drovr:verification-before-completion`**.
- Reviewing an artifact (code, spec, plan) → **`drovr:code-review`**. Per the
  *Always review* rule above, this runs on every change — not only before shipping.

## Escalation contract — inline first

**Default: do the work inline in this session.** Do not reach for phases for a
task that fits. Escalate only when a single context cannot hold the work well.

- **Primary signal — context fullness.** If the transcript is filling to the
  point where output would rot, escalate.
- **Secondary heuristic** (a proxy for the above, not a hard rule): roughly
  **10+ files** touched, or **3+ independent work items**.

When you must escalate, pick the smallest tool that fits:

- **Mid-flight escape hatch — author a HANDOFF yourself.** You are deep in a task
  and this context is filling. You have the whole session in context, so compress
  it *yourself*: write a `HANDOFF.md` (the 7-section shape from `drovr:handoff`,
  git pointers included), then continue in a fresh agent seeded from it. Nothing
  compresses it for you — the finishing agent always authors its own handoff.
- **A single planned boundary → `drovr:handoff`.** Hand finished work across one
  phase boundary to a fresh clean-context agent.
- **A full gated run → `drovr:pipeline`.** Brainstorm → plan → implement → review
  with a human approval gate on `spec.md` before any code is written.

**Putting *any* spec/design in front of a human for approval — even a one-off, not a
full pipeline — goes through the review gate, and the gate has two halves you must run
together:** `drovr review summary <run> "<what changed>"` to present `spec.md`, **and** a
backgrounded `drovr review wait <run>` — the *watch*. (The server itself is global and
always-on: `drovr serve` takes **no** run argument and auto-starts on demand, so serving is not
a step you perform per run.) `summary` opens the gate and prints the reviewer's page URL plus
the exact watch command; it does **not** start the watch. Without the watch you never learn the
decision and fall back to hand-polling `GET /state` (the anti-pattern).
`review wait` blocks on the gate and the harness wakes you when the reviewer acts
(exit `0` approved · `3` request-changes + `feedback.json` · `5` cancelled — the human
abandoned the run, stop · `2` timeout, re-run · `1` error, which is **never** an approval).
Revise loop: edit `spec.md` →
`drovr review summary <run> "<what changed>"` → re-background `review wait`. Full mechanics
(state machine, diff baselining, gotchas) live in `drovr:pipeline` → "The spec gate".

**REQUIRED BACKGROUND:** the downstream skills assume this file's contracts —
single-writer rule, the run dir at `~/.local/share/drovr/runs/<name>/`, and that
**drovr composes every brief; you supply only context.** `drovr phase start <run>
<phase> --context "<what this phase needs that drovr cannot know>"` composes the
phase's brief and injects it. Never write the frame yourself: `drovr phase brief`
prints what an agent will be told, and `drovr code-review brief … --angle <angle>`
does the same for a reviewer you spawn in-harness. `phase send` remains for
free-form nudges — a message is not a brief.
</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>",

content.text:
Found the cause. Two facts first:

1. **Your keyring is locked and nothing unlocks it.** `~/.local/share/keyrings/Default_keyring.keyring` is password-protected, there is no `pam_gnome_keyring` in any `/etc/pam.d/*` stack, so every libsecret client triggers a `gcr-prompter` popup. Journal shows dozens today, all cancelled.
2. **TPM won't help you.** You aren't in the `tss` group (`/dev/tpmrm0` is `root:tss 0660`, unreadable), and more importantly a TPM-sealed passphrase unseals for *anything running as you* — same threat model as no password at all. Your home is already homed/LUKS-encrypted, so TPM adds ~nothing on top. `ssh-tpm-agent.service` isn't even loaded right now.

**The better lever:** homed already makes you type your password at tty login. `pam_gnome_keyring.so` is installed at `/usr/lib/security/`. Wire it in and the keyring unlocks with the password you already type — zero popups, keyring stays genuinely encrypted at rest.

Side finding: your systemd `--user` manager is poisoned again this boot (`UnitPath=/.config/systemd/user`), so HM's `gnome-keyring.service` and `ssh-tpm-agent.service` are invisible; Arch's packaged unit is serving secrets instead. Separate issue — flagging it, not fixing it here.

options.label: pam_gnome_keyring (Recommended)
options.description: Add auth+session pam_gnome_keyring.so to the login PAM stack, rename the keyring to `login`, set its password to your login password. Keyring stays encrypted; unlocks silently at tty login. Exit code 1
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Run as your normal user (e.g. `mise run deploy`), NOT under sudo: the sops
# steps below decrypt with your GCP key under $HOME and each privileged install
# sudo's itself. Running the whole script as root points $HOME at /root, so sops
# can't find the key (and root has no KMS creds) -- fail fast instead.
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "system/deploy: run as your user (try 'mise run system:deploy'), not root." >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$(dirname "$0")"
find etc/ -type d | while read -r d; do sudo mkdir -p "/${d}"; done
find etc/ -type f | while read -r f; do sudo cp -v "${f}" "/${f}"; done

# polkit only scans /usr/share/polkit-1/actions for action definitions, which
# etc/ can't reach; install Bitwarden's unlock action there so its "system
# authentication" biometric prompt is authorized on this non-NixOS host.
sudo install -Dvm644 polkit-1/actions/com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.policy \
  /usr/share/polkit-1/actions/com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.policy

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now systemd-oomd

# ── attic binary cache: make nix read nix.custom.conf + render the pull token ──
# nix.custom.conf adds attic.ko.ag/kube as an extra substituter; the cache is
# PRIVATE, so the nix daemon needs a read token. We are not a nix `trusted-user`,
# so both the config and the token must reach the daemon at the system level.
#
#   • Determinate Nix auto-`!include`s nix.custom.conf from /etc/nix/nix.conf and
#     merges /etc/determinate/netrc.custom (via config.json) into its netrc.
#   • Plain upstream nix (e.g. utsuho) does neither, so we wire it up here:
#       - ensure /etc/nix/nix.conf `!include`s nix.custom.conf (idempotent)
#       - render the token to /etc/nix/netrc, the daemon's default netrc-file
#     (On a Determinate host the extra /etc/nix/netrc copy is simply unused.)
# The token is sops-encrypted in ../secrets.yaml: decrypt as the user (GCP KMS),
# then install to /etc as root. The token is never printed.
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="${GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS:-$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json}"

# Plain upstream nix only reads /etc/nix/nix.conf; pull in nix.custom.conf so the
# substituter + trusted key take effect. Idempotent, and a no-op on Determinate
# (whose own nix.conf already includes it, so the grep matches and we skip).
if ! sudo grep -qF 'nix.custom.conf' /etc/nix/nix.conf 2>/dev/null; then
  echo '!include nix.custom.conf' | sudo tee -a /etc/nix/nix.conf >/dev/null

set -euo pipefail

# Run as your normal user (e.g. `mise run deploy`), NOT under sudo: the sops
# steps below decrypt with your GCP key under $HOME and each privileged install
# sudo's itself. Running the whole script as root points $HOME at /root, so sops
# can't find the key (and root has no KMS creds) -- fail fast instead.
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "system/deploy: run as your user (try 'mise run system:deploy'), not root." >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$(dirname "$0")"
find etc/ -type d | while read -r d; do sudo mkdir -p "/${d}"; done
find etc/ -type f | while read -r f; do sudo cp -v "${f}" "/${f}"; done

# polkit only scans /usr/share/polkit-1/actions for action definitions, which
# etc/ can't reach; install Bitwarden's unlock action there so its "system
# authentication" biometric prompt is authorized on this non-NixOS host.
sudo install -Dvm644 polkit-1/actions/com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.policy \
  /usr/share/polkit-1/actions/com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.policy

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now systemd-oomd

# ── attic binary cache: make nix read nix.custom.conf + render the pull token ──
# nix.custom.conf adds attic.ko.ag/kube as an extra substituter; the cache is
# PRIVATE, so the nix daemon needs a read token. We are not a nix `trusted-user`,
# so both the config and the token must reach the daemon at the system level.
#
#   • Determinate Nix auto-`!include`s nix.custom.conf from /etc/nix/nix.conf and
#     merges /etc/determinate/netrc.custom (via config.json) into its netrc.
#   • Plain upstream nix (e.g. utsuho) does neither, so we wire it up here:
#       - ensure /etc/nix/nix.conf `!include`s nix.custom.conf (idempotent)
#       - render the token to /etc/nix/netrc, the daemon's default netrc-file
#     (On a Determinate host the extra /etc/nix/netrc copy is simply unused.)
# The token is sops-encrypted in ../secrets.yaml: decrypt as the user (GCP KMS),
# then install to /etc as root. The token is never printed.
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="${GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS:-$HOME/.config/sops/gcp-key.json}"

# Plain upstream nix only reads /etc/nix/nix.conf; pull in nix.custom.conf so the
# substituter + trusted key take effect. Idempotent, and a no-op on Determinate
# (whose own nix.conf already includes it, so the grep matches and we skip).
if ! sudo grep -qF 'nix.custom.conf' /etc/nix/nix.conf 2>/dev/null; then
  echo '!include nix.custom.conf' | sudo tee -a /etc/nix/nix.conf >/dev/null
fi

sops -d --extract '["atticPullToken"]' ../secrets.yaml \
  | sed 's#^#machine attic.ko.ag password #' \
  | sudo install -m600 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/determinate/netrc.custom
sops -d --extract '["atticPullToken"]' ../secrets.yaml \
  | sed 's#^#machine attic.ko.ag password #' \
  | sudo install -m600 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/nix/netrc

# ── remote builder: SSH key the nix daemon uses to reach mari ─────────────────
# nix.custom.conf delegates aarch64-darwin builds to sauyon@mari-1 over Tailscale;
# the daemon (root) authenticates with this key. Private key is sops-encrypted in
# ../secrets.yaml; install root-owned, 0600. Never printed.
sops -d --extract '["mariBuilderKey"]' ../secrets.yaml \
  | sudo install -m600 -o root -g root /dev/stdin /etc/nix/mari-builder-key

# Pick up the new substituter, trusted key, netrc, and builder.
sudo systemctl restart nix-daemon

# ── tailscaled: patched build from this flake (Linux only) ───────────────────
# Tailscale SSH calls logind CreateSession before the user's shell runs, so for a
# systemd-homed user whose LUKS home is still locked it starts user@<uid>.service
# against homed's fallback home ("/") and permanently breaks that user manager's
# unit search path for the rest of the boot. The patch makes tailscaled ask homed
# for the user's state first and skip session creation when the home isn't active.
# See ../patches/tailscale-ssh-skip-logind-session-for-locked-homed-user.patch
#
# Build as the invoking user (root's nix may lack flakes and our substituters),
# then have root pin the result. A symlink placed directly in /nix/var/nix/gcroots
# is a permanent GC root, and we reuse it as the stable path tailscaled.service
# references -- it must resolve at boot, i.e. outside the encrypted home.
if [[ "$(uname -s)" == Linux ]]; then
  ts_out="$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths "$(cd .. && pwd)#tailscale-patched")"
  sudo ln -sfn "${ts_out}" /nix/var/nix/gcroots/tailscale-patched
  # The CLI too: /usr/bin/tailscale belongs to the distro package, which this
  # replaces. The wrapper dispatches on argv[0], so a symlink named `tailscale`
  # gets CLI behaviour rather than the daemon.
  sudo install -d /usr/local/bin
  sudo ln -sfn /nix/var/nix/gcroots/tailscale-patched/bin/tailscale /usr/local/bin/tailscale
  sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  sudo systemctl restart tailscaled
fi

passphrase, so it is replaced by a unit of the same name whose ExecStart is a
wrapper that unseals and feeds the daemon on stdin.

long before graphical-session-pre.target, and would otherwise win the
org.freedesktop.secrets bus name with a locked collection.

unseal the passphrase, exactly as with an empty one. The gain over a passphraseless
keyring is only that the keyring file is useless off this machine. The passphrase

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Run as your normal user (e.g. `mise run deploy`), NOT under sudo: the sops
# steps below decrypt with your GCP key under $HOME and each privileged install
# sudo's itself. Running the whole script as root points $HOME at /root, so sops
# can't find the key (and root has no KMS creds) -- fail fast instead.
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "system/deploy: run as your user (try 'mise run system:deploy'), not root." >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$(dirname "$0")"
find etc/ -type d | while read -r d; do sudo mkdir -p "/${d}"; done
find etc/ -type f | while read -r f; do sudo cp -v "${f}" "/${f}"; done

# polkit only scans /usr/share/polkit-1/actions for action definitions, which
# etc/ can't reach; install Bitwarden's unlock action there so its "system
# authentication" biometric prompt is authorized on this non-NixOS host.
sudo install -Dvm644 polkit-1/actions/com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.policy \
  /usr/share/polkit-1/actions/com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.policy

# The keyring's login collection can only be unlocked at daemon startup, so
# home-manager runs its own gnome-keyring.service whose ExecStart unseals the
# passphrase from the TPM (see gnome-keyring-tpm in home.nix). Arch's packaged

# every libsecret client gets an unlock popup again. Mask both units so only the
# home-manager one can start. (Symptom if this regresses: two
# gnome-keyring-daemon processes, and `busctl --user status
# org.freedesktop.secrets` naming the one from gnome-keyring-daemon.service.)
sudo rm -f /etc/systemd/user/sockets.target.wants/gnome-keyring-daemon.socket
sudo ln -sfn /dev/null /etc/systemd/user/gnome-keyring-daemon.socket

# Takes effect at next login, not in the current session.
if ! id -nG "$USER" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -qx tss; then

fi

sudo systemctl enable --now systemd-oomd

# nix.custom.conf adds attic.ko.ag/kube as an extra substituter; the cache is

#       - render the token to /etc/nix/netrc, the daemon's default netrc-file

# Tailscale SSH calls logind CreateSession before the user's shell runs, so for a
# systemd-homed user whose LUKS home is still locked it starts user@<uid>.service
# against homed's fallback home ("/") and permanently breaks that user manager's
# unit search path for the rest of the boot. The patch makes tailscaled ask homed
# for the user's state first and skip session creation when the home isn't active.
# See ../patches/tailscale-ssh-skip-logind-session-for-locked-homed-user.patch

# Build as the invoking user (root's nix may lack flakes and our substituters),
# then have root pin the result. A symlink placed directly in /nix/var/nix/gcroots
# is a permanent GC root, and we reuse it as the stable path tailscaled.service
# references -- it must resolve at boot, i.e. outside the encrypted home.

  sudo ln -sfn /nix/var/nix/gcroots/tailscale-patched/bin/tailscale /usr/local/bin/tailscale
  sudo systemctl daemon-reload
  sudo systemctl restart tailscaled
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Run as your normal user (e.g. `mise run deploy`), NOT under sudo: the sops
# steps below decrypt with your GCP key under $HOME and each privileged install
# sudo's itself. Running the whole script as root points $HOME at /root, so sops
# can't find the key (and root has no KMS creds) -- fail fast instead.
if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "system/deploy: run as your user (try 'mise run system:deploy'), not root." >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$(dirname "$0")"
find etc/ -type d | while read -r d; do sudo mkdir -p "/${d}"; done
find etc/ -type f | while read -r f; do sudo cp -v "${f}" "/${f}"; done

# etc/ can't reach; install Bitwarden's unlock action there so its "system
# authentication" biometric prompt is authorized on this non-NixOS host.
sudo install -Dvm644 polkit-1/actions/com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.policy \
  /usr/share/polkit-1/actions/com.bitwarden.Bitwarden.policy

# Takes effect at next login, not in the current session.
if ! id -nG "$USER" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -qx tss; then
  sudo gpasswd -a "$USER" tss
fi

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now systemd-oomd

# ── attic binary cache: make nix read nix.custom.conf + render the pull token ──
# nix.custom.conf adds attic.ko.ag/kube as an extra substituter; the cache is
# PRIVATE, so the nix daemon needs a read token. We are not a nix `trusted-user`,
# so both the config and the token must reach the daemon at the system level.
#
#   • Determinate Nix auto-`!include`s nix.custom.conf from /etc/nix/nix.conf and
#     merges /etc/determinate/netrc.custom (via config.json) into its netrc.
#   • Plain upstream nix (e.g. utsuho) does neither, so we wire it up here:
#       - ensure /etc/nix/nix.conf `!include`s nix.custom.conf (idempotent)
#       - render the token to /etc/nix/netrc, the daemon's default netrc-file
#     (On a Determinate host the extra /etc/nix/netrc copy is simply unused.)
# The token is sops-encrypted in ../secrets.yaml: decrypt as the user (GCP KMS),

fi

# nix.custom.conf delegates aarch64-darwin builds to sauyon@mari-1 over Tailscale;
# the daemon (root) authenticates with this key. Private key is sops-encrypted in
# ../secrets.yaml; install root-owned, 0600. Never printed.

# Tailscale SSH calls logind CreateSession before the user's shell runs, so for a
# systemd-homed user whose LUKS home is still locked it starts user@<uid>.service
# against homed's fallback home ("/") and permanently breaks that user manager's
# unit search path for the rest of the boot. The patch makes tailscaled ask homed
# for the user's state first and skip session creation when the home isn't active.
# See ../patches/tailscale-ssh-skip-logind-session-for-locked-homed-user.patch
#
# Build as the invoking user (root's nix may lack flakes and our substituters),
# then have root pin the result. A symlink placed directly in /nix/var/nix/gcroots
# is a permanent GC root, and we reuse it as the stable path tailscaled.service
# references -- it must resolve at boot, i.e. outside the encrypted home.
if [[ "$(uname -s)" == Linux ]]; then

  sudo ln -sfn /nix/var/nix/gcroots/tailscale-patched/bin/tailscale /usr/local/bin/tailscale
  sudo systemctl daemon-reload

fi
